title: Token Sentinel: Cost Orbit & Attribution Explorer — compact export flow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need a concise way to understand token-level cost distribution across models, routes, and accounts and to export role-aware line items for billing reconciliation. Current console views are table-heavy and require multiple downloads + manual aggregation.

Goal: Deliver a compact, scannable visualization — the 'Cost Orbit' — that surfaces per-route and per-model token spend, enables quick attribution (top contributors, anomalies), and supports multi-format exports (CSV, normalized ledger JSON) with role-aware presets for finance or platform SRE teams. Provide an interactive prototype to validate information density, export schema, and edge-case handling for very large accounts.

Proposed solution summary:
- Visual: Radial "orbit" view where the center is the selected scope (account/org or project). Orbits represent hierarchical buckets (model family -> model variant -> route). Arc width = cost share; color = category (generation vs embedding vs system tokens). Hover reveals time-sliced mini-histogram and sample prompt footprints.
- Controls: Time range slider (absolute or rolling), aggregation toggle (per-invocation vs per-token cost), normalization selector (USD vs CPU-equivalent), and attribution lens (by model, by route, by user/team).
- Export: Export presets: Finance (line-item CSV with invoice mapping), Platform (normalized JSON with model commit/version, quantization profile, and runtime id), Audit (CSV + hash manifest). Exports can be scoped by selection (orbit wedge) and include optional prompt redaction/obfuscation.
- Accessibility & scale: Provide alternative table+sparkline view for screen readers and large datasets, and a pagination/streaming export mechanism for >10M tokens to avoid timeouts.

Design trade-offs considered:
1) Visual density vs clarity — orbit supports compactness but may be unfamiliar; we pair it with immediate table fallback and onboarding tooltip.
2) Performance — client-side rendering for small scopes, server-rendered tile caches for enterprise scopes.
3) Export schema complexity — provide a minimal canonical CSV + optional rich JSON to satisfy both finance and engineering.

Notes on alignment with product & infra: The view should reuse existing metrics APIs (token counts, cost per-model) and subscribe to the console's role-aware permission layer to gate exports and redaction. The prototype assumes new backend endpoints for paginated export and a normalized invoice mapping layer (see dependencies).
updates: 2026-02-14: Initial sketch and concept walkthrough with PM and Eng. Riley suggested adding 'prompt sample on hover' to help debug high-cost wedges.
2026-02-18: Hi-fi Figma prototype v0.1 created (orbit + fallback list). Shared with Analytics team for performance constraints.
2026-02-22: PM (Miguel Ortega) requested export presets be saved to org defaults and surfaced in Billing settings.
2026-02-25: Eng (Samira Khan) flagged pagination requirement for exports >5M tokens; added streaming export flows to spec.
2026-02-27: Design critique: prefer stronger contrast for generation vs embedding colors; a11y reviewer requested keyboard-first interactions for wedge selection.
2026-03-01: Prototype updated with accessibility tab order, export manifest schema draft attached. Ready for stakeholder review.
comments: Miguel Ortega (PM): Love the compactness. Please add a 'cost per 1k tokens' tooltip and a way to pin a wedge to follow over time.
Samira Khan (Eng): Backend needs: (1) paginated export API, (2) per-wedge pre-aggregation to avoid heavy realtime joins. We'll prototype a cache TTL and test with synthetic traces.

Riley Chen (Design owner): Add onboarding microcopy to explain orbit layers and provide a one-click 'export visible' action. Consider micro-animations to help discoverability but allow opt-out for users with motion sensitivity.

Finance reviewer (Evan Brooks): CSV invoice mapping must include customer_id, route_path, model_tag, tokens_in, tokens_out, unit_price, total_price, and optional pricing_slab_id. Recommend default header order for downstream ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Orbit visualization implemented in prototype with hover state showing mini time-histogram and sample prompts (Figma + storybook).
Fallback table view available and accessible by keyboard/screen reader with same export behaviors.
Export presets: Finance, Platform, Audit implemented as export modal options; exported CSV matches invoice mapping spec and JSON contains normalized runtime metadata.
Backend export API: supports streaming exports for scopes up to 100M tokens and returns a manifest with checksum and line count.
Design review sign-off from PM, Eng lead, and Finance on export schema and redaction policy.
